_note: Recurring-series programming for The Lecture Hall (channels/publish.php; see docs/series-and-channels.md and channels/publish/README.md). Nine blocks, each one real complete lecture per daily occurrence -- packing.enabled is deliberately NOT used anywhere here: lectures run 20-150+ minutes and packing exists to fit several SHORT episodes into one fixed slot, which fights 'respect real lecture durations' and 'air a structured lecture series in its intended order' for long-form content (see docs/series-and-channels.md's packing section and this task's own brief). Block spacing was chosen from each series' real approved-episode duration range (see series/<id>/series.json), not from the nominal 'duration' field -- ProgrammingCompiler/BoundaryResolver only ever compare a real episode's actual end against the NEXT occurrence's real calendar start time (channels/publish/src/ProgrammingCompiler.php's own header, point (b)); 'duration' itself is just a fallback for an episode with no known duration. Every block below still carries a comfortable margin between its own longest approved episode and the next block's start, PLUS an explicit boundary.mode='soft' + max_delay as a second line of defense for future refreshes that might approve a longer episode -- except 'history-and-civilization' and 'the-evening-lecture', which keep boundary.mode='hard' (the default) because their source material (Yale's ~46-54min classes; Gresham's ~29-67min public lectures) has either very low variance or a very large trailing gap before the next block, so hard was evaluated and is genuinely safe, matching Science & Engineering's own precedent for when to prefer hard. 'stanford-cs229' is intentionally not scheduled anywhere here (see catalog.json's _note: 16/17 of its imported videos are not embeddable).
